Simulate a pedigree with deaths, emigration and immigration

Source: R/sim_pop.R
sim_pop.Rd

Simulates an individual-based population over discrete time steps and returns the complete pedigree together with the step at which each individual arrived and left. It is meant for testing and benchmarking rel_add() and rel_remove(), since the number of individuals alive stays roughly constant while the pedigree keeps growing.

Usage

sim_pop(
  n_steps = 50,
  n_init = 100,
  K = 2 * n_init,
  maturity = 2,
  p_birth = 0.6,
  p_death = 0.1,
  p_emigrate = 0.02,
  n_immigrants = 1
)

Arguments

n_steps

Number of time steps after step 0.

n_init

Number of founders at step 0.

K

Carrying capacity: the birth probability decreases linearly to 0 when the number of individuals alive, N, reaches it.

maturity

Number of steps after birth before an individual can reproduce or emigrate. Founders and immigrants are mature on arrival.

p_birth

Maximum probability that a mature female reproduces in a step (one offspring at most per step).

p_death

Probability of death per step.

p_emigrate

Probability of emigration per step for mature individuals that did not die.

n_immigrants

Mean number of immigrants per step (Poisson).

Value

A data frame with one row per individual ever present, in order of arrival, so parents always come before their offspring, and with columns:

  • id, dadid, momid: identifiers (NA for unknown parents);

  • sex: 1 = male, 2 = female;

  • arrival: step at which the individual enters the pedigree (0 for founders);

  • exit: step at which it leaves, NA if it is still present at the end;

  • fate: "dead", "emigrated" or NA;

  • origin: "founder", "born" or "immigrant".

Details

Step 0 creates n_init adult founders with unknown parents. At each following step t:

  1. Each mature female alive at the start of the step reproduces with probability p_birth * (1 - N / K) (bounded to [0, 1]), where N is the number of individuals alive. The father is drawn at random among the mature males (NA if there is none). Newborns arrive at step t.

  2. A Poisson number (mean n_immigrants) of adult immigrants with unknown parents arrive at step t.

  3. Each individual that was alive at the start of the step dies with probability p_death, and otherwise, if mature, emigrates with probability p_emigrate. Its exit is t.

Newborns and immigrants cannot leave in the step in which they arrive, and parents are always alive at the start of the step in which their offspring are born. Therefore, replaying the steps in order with rel_add() for the arrivals followed by rel_remove() for the exits never refers to an unknown individual or to a removed parent (see the example).

The result depends on the state of the random number generator of the session: call set.seed() beforehand to make it reproducible.

See also

sim_ped(), rel_remove()

Examples

set.seed(2)
pop <- sim_pop(n_steps = 40, n_init = 60)
table(pop$origin)
#> 
#>      born   founder immigrant 
#>       271        60        45 
table(pop$fate, useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#>      dead emigrated      <NA> 
#>       271        43        62 

## replay the simulation with the incremental store
rel <- rel_new()
size <- integer(41)
for (t in 0:40) {
  rel_add(rel, pop[pop$arrival == t, ])   # the columns needed are found by name
  rel_remove(rel, pop$id[!is.na(pop$exit) & pop$exit == t])
  size[t + 1] <- rel_size(rel)
}
size
#>  [1] 60 62 58 58 52 55 55 59 60 60 61 65 67 73 78 75 73 78 79 74 72 77 68 70 66
#> [26] 70 70 71 71 69 64 67 58 67 70 65 65 63 61 61 62

## the survivors agree with the relatedness computed from the whole pedigree
A <- fastrel_ped(pop)
alive <- rel_ids(rel)
all.equal(rel_get(rel), A[alive, alive])
#> [1] TRUE
